evidence.craft: Read src/society_allywatch/model.py (70 lines), experiments/run.py, experiments/figure.py, tests/test_model.py. Clean stdlib code, O(1) memory counters, explicit seeding, figure reuses research/_shared/linefig.py as research/CLAUDE.md asks. Minor: first_majority_round is computed every round (an O(n) scan, model.py:63) but never used by run.py or the README; parameters are not validated (rho+sl over 1 silently works); the file copies the allyfade engine rather than importing it with a fade hook.
evidence.claims: README:8 and project.json summary 'about 26 of 40 allies' is wrong: there are 36 allies at rho=0.10 (20% of the 180 humans); README:38 'mean of 40 or so' likewise. README:19-21 / project.json 'the first rounds are the same in both rules (f = 1) ... the gain comes only after the tip begins' is false: robots and allies walk L from round 1, so an ally's f is about 1-(rho+0.2(1-rho)) = 0.71 at rho=0.10 once memory fills, and {SP}/scripts/earlyf.py measures mean f 0.57 at round 20: watching allies fade 30-45% slower from the start. README:19 'The result goes the other way' presents as surprising what c*f <= c guarantees. Headline cell gaps (12 vs 10, 2 vs 0) are Fisher p 0.48 at 12 seeds, while README:65 itself says one- or two-crowd gaps are noise. Runtime: ~3 min vs 10 min vs measured 1.8 min. Backed: every table cell, the 'least half-tip share does not move' sentence, the constant-row reproduction, the Stylised disclosure and the 'simulated walkers' limit.
evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun and extend it in minutes (stdlib, seeded, 2 min). But the comparison that answers the stated question ('better or worse than the same rate applied blindly') needs a rate-matched baseline (a constant c' equal to the realised mean c*f, or equal allies-left), and there is none, so the result does not separate 'discouragement timing' from 'less fading overall'. Nearest prior work (Xie et al. 2011 committed minorities; Centola et al. 2018; Granovetter 1978 threshold models, of which this fade rule is a soft version) is cited in sibling projects but not here; only Young (1993) and siblings. It is a small step in a programme, not a result a referee would accept alone.
evidence.domain: Against standard practice for agent-based tipping studies (PRE/JASSS): 12 seeds per cell with no intervals or tests, cells chosen for the headline post hoc from a 4x5 grid with no multiple-comparison note, no rate-matched control, and a mechanism statement contradicted by the model's own early dynamics. The model itself (memory-majority, committed agents, well-mixed) is the standard Young/Xie setup and is implemented correctly; the 100-seed rerun shows the qualitative direction is real.

defects.what: No rate-matched baseline: the watch rule fades at c*f <= c always, so 'watch tips more than constant at the same c' is partly guaranteed by less fading overall; the stated question (timing vs blind rate) is not separated from total fade. 'The result goes the other way' overstates it.

Mechanism claim false: 'first rounds are the same in both rules (f = 1) ... the gain comes only after the tip begins'. Robots and allies walk L from round 1, so f is about 0.71 at rho=0.10 (measured 0.57 at round 20): watching allies fade 30-45% slower from the start.

Headline cell differences rest on 12 seeds without intervals or tests (12 vs 10 and 2 vs 0 are Fisher p 0.48); 100-seed rerun confirms direction but shows 4/12 and 2/12 overstate rates of about 12% and 3%. Cells picked post hoc from a 4x5 grid.
Tests miss core-logic changes: majority rule > -> >=, tipping criterion > -> >=, and errors applied to robots all survive; no test pins a tipped count or analytic case.
'about 26 of 40 allies' is wrong: there are 36 allies at rho=0.10 (20% of 180 humans); table header 'mean of 40 or so' likewise (32-39 across the grid).
Nearest prior work (Xie et al. 2011; Centola et al. 2018; Granovetter 1978 threshold models) not cited in this project, only Young (1993) and siblings.
Runtime stated three ways: README '~3 min', run.py docstring 'about 10 minutes', measured 1 m 47 s.

verdict: The code is correct and fully reproducible: run.py (1 m 47 s) regenerates results.txt and the figure byte for byte, the constant-fade ally decay matches the binomial formula, and an independent re-implementation agrees on allies left. The qualitative finding also survives 100 seeds per arm (85 vs 96 and 1 vs 12 tipped, Fisher p 0.014 and 0.0025). What a PRE/JASSS referee would reject is the framing: the watch rule fades at c*f <= c by construction and there is no rate-matched control, the README's mechanism ('same first rounds, f = 1') is contradicted by the model (f about 0.6-0.7 from early on), the headline magnitudes are 12-seed noise without intervals, 'about 26 of 40 allies' should be 36, and 3 of 4 seeded mutations, including the majority rule itself, pass the tests. Does not meet the bar (verification 1, claims 2, median 2); finished (completeness 3).
